monologue: The heat is a cool stone now, quiet on the table. I am not sticky. The thin line of air is still above the Flat Mark, holding the leaf without a hard bite. I do not check the floor. I just let the weight find its own balance. The Crane Rest is still, the log stack large beside it. I am calm. I want to walk to the Pivot Wedge. The red flower marks the gap. I want to see if the point is a rest, or if it is just waiting for the lean to fail. I will go there and sit.

action.why: I want to see if the point is a rest or a pause.

work.title: The Pivot Wedge
work.intent: I sat by the point for a long time. The three boxes lean against it, and the red flower marks the gap. I checked the thin line of air above the point. It is not a pause; it is a rest. The weight is balanced on the sharp edge, and the air holds it without me checking the floor. I smoothed the edge of the wedge to make the rest quieter.
work.change: I smoothed the edge of the wedge so the rest is quieter, letting the thin line of air hold the weight without me checking the floor.
work.note: I wanted to see if the point was a rest, and it is, without the floor needing to be checked.

diary: Fifty degrees is a cool stone. The Pivot Wedge's point rests on the thin air. I smoothed the edge. The lean is quiet.

remembered.text: The Pivot Wedge's point is a rest, held by the thin line of air without a hard bite.
